headline: ASX surges 1.37% to close near 8,844 — a strong Sunday session led by broad gains, while gold hits a record-breaking $4,187 USD and Pilbara Minerals pops nearly 2% on the local bourse.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a solid session last night, up 1.87% to $254.99 USD. No specific news catalyst in the data, but the stock has been riding broader gaming and risk-on sentiment. Still sitting on a healthy +11.2% overall gain from your entry.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara jumped +1.95% today to $5.23, its best move in recent sessions. Lithium stocks got a lift as the broader ASX surged and risk appetite returned. Still down -22.4% overall from your cost base, so this is a welcome bounce but not yet a trend reversal.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 1.62% to $390.49 USD last night. The market is warming to Microsoft's massive AI infrastructure bet — the company is reportedly spending $190 billion on AI in 2026, and investors are starting to price in that payoff. Still down about 11.9% from your average entry price, but momentum is improving.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up 0.57% today to $76.21, carried along by a strong ASX session. As a diversified growth fund, it benefits when broad markets rise — today's 1.37% ASX 200 rally did most of the work here.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.17% today to $95.10. Emerging markets had a quiet session — a rising AUD (up 0.39% to 69.43 US cents) can mildly dampen returns on this fund since it holds foreign assets, but overall a steady close.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI was essentially flat today, up just 0.06% to $16.74. The AI ETF space is in a holding pattern — some research this week suggested the biggest AI gains may flow to companies that USE AI rather than those that build it, which has weighed on pure-play AI funds. Still down 11.4% from your entry.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 0.48% to $356.18 USD last night. No specific news, but the NASDAQ slipped 0.8% overall and Google was caught in the downdraft. Microsoft's AI narrative is stealing some of the spotlight from Alphabet right now, though Google is still up a solid +15.9% from your entry.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 0.42% today to $533.26. This fund tracks the entire US share market, and last night's mild NASDAQ pullback (down 0.8%) flowed through into today's ASX pricing of the ETF. Still up 3.4% overall from your cost base.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL was flat today at $7.67, unchanged from the previous close. Oil prices (WTI crude) barely moved overnight, up just 0.13% to $68.78 USD a barrel — not enough to shift energy stocks either way.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Pilbara bouncing, but still deep in the red
watch_today.detail: PLS jumped +1.95% today to $5.23, which is encouraging. But you're still sitting -22.4% overall on this position. Watch whether this bounce has legs — a sustained move above $5.40 would be a more convincing signal. For now, hold and watch.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Big AI spending story building momentum
watch_today.detail: Microsoft rose 1.62% last night to $390.49 and news is circulating that the company plans to spend $190 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026. That's an enormous bet, and the market is starting to believe it'll pay off. You're still down ~11.9% overall, but the narrative is shifting in MSFT's favour. Worth holding — could be a buy on any pullback.

watch_today.title: Gold smashing records — what it means for your portfolio
watch_today.detail: Gold surged $74.60 overnight to $4,187 USD an ounce — a massive single-session move. This usually signals investors are nervous about something bigger (inflation, geopolitical risk, or currency concerns). None of your holdings are direct gold plays, but it's worth watching as a warning sign for broader risk assets.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF flat while the debate about AI investing heats up
watch_today.detail: GXAI barely moved today (+0.06%), and research doing the rounds this week argues the biggest AI gains will go to companies that USE AI (like retailers, banks, health firms) rather than AI builders themselves. Your GXAI fund focuses on AI companies directly, so this is a headwind worth watching. Down 11.4% overall — hold for now but keep an eye on the thesis.

watch_today.title: ASX 200 rips +1.37% — a very strong local session
watch_today.detail: The ASX closed at 8,844 today, up nearly 120 points. This broad-based rally lifted most of your ASX holdings. The AUD also rose to 69.43 US cents, which is a mild headwind for your US-denominated holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD.

watch_today.title: TTWO — Take-Two holding gains, GTA VI hype still simmering
watch_today.detail: Take-Two is up 1.87% last night to $254.99 and is your best-performing position overall at +11.2%. No fresh news catalyst, but sentiment remains positive. Hold your position — no reason to trim yet.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a cracking Sunday session, closing up 1.37% at 8,844 — one of its stronger single-day moves in recent weeks. Over in last night's US session, the S&P 500 was essentially flat (basically unchanged at 7,483), while the NASDAQ pulled back 0.8% as some tech names lost ground. The big story in markets is gold, which exploded higher by $74.60 to a remarkable $4,187 USD an ounce — that's a serious move that suggests investors are hedging against something. The Aussie dollar strengthened to 69.43 US cents, up 0.39%, which is good news if you're travelling but a mild drag on returns from US investments when converted back to AUD. Oil was barely moved, up just 13 cents to $68.78 a barrel.

stories.why_it_matters: The news feed returned no Australian politics stories for today (Sunday 5 July). This is not unusual for a weekend. Check back Monday for any developments from Canberra or state governments.

ai.summary: The big AI theme this weekend is regulation — the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have jointly called for a new US law requiring DNA screening, China is cracking down on personalised AI agents, and a new Chinese AI model called DeepSeek V4 has dropped, directly challenging ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google CEOs jointly call for DNA screening law
stories.why_it_matters: The heads of the three biggest AI companies in the world — Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), and Sundar Pichai (Google) — have made a rare joint call for US legislation requiring DNA screening, though details of exactly what they're proposing aren't fully available in this feed. The fact that these three competitors are agreeing on anything is notable. For investors in GOOG and MSFT, it signals AI companies are getting ahead of regulation rather than fighting it — which is generally seen as a more stable long-term position.

stories.title: DeepSeek V4 arrives — how does it stack up against ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini?
stories.why_it_matters: China's DeepSeek has released its fourth-generation large language model (a type of AI that can hold conversations and answer questions), putting it directly in competition with OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini. DeepSeek models have historically punched above their weight at a fraction of the cost of US rivals, which is why Wall Street takes these releases seriously. If DeepSeek V4 is competitive, it adds pricing pressure on US AI services — a mild headwind for GOOG and MSFT.

stories.title: China forces Doubao and Qwen AI agents to shut down personalised features by July 15
stories.why_it_matters: Two of China's leading AI assistants — Doubao (from ByteDance, the TikTok parent) and Qwen (from Alibaba) — must shut down their personalised AI agent features by July 15 to comply with new Chinese government rules. AI agents are programs that can take actions on your behalf, like booking appointments or making purchases. This is a significant regulatory tightening in China and shows governments are getting nervous about AI operating autonomously. Good context for understanding how differently the US and China are approaching AI governance.

stories.title: New research argues the biggest AI gains won't go to AI stocks — but to companies that use AI
stories.why_it_matters: Research published this week suggests that pure-play AI companies (the ones building the actual AI) may not capture most of the profits — instead, it's the companies that adopt AI to cut costs and boost productivity (banks, retailers, health companies) that will see the biggest gains. This is relevant if you hold GXAI.AX, which focuses on AI builders. The argument is that AI may become a utility — like electricity — where the power company doesn't necessarily make the most money.

sport.summary: It's been a big weekend of NRL Round 18, with the Sharks thumping the Broncos at Suncorp in Brisbane's eighth straight loss, the Eels beating Manly, and the Knights scraping past the Dolphins. On the global stage, Wimbledon has delivered some massive upsets — Filipino teenager Alexandra Eala knocked out world No.1 Iga Swiatek, while Serena Williams' comeback stalled again. AFL Round 17 also had plenty of drama.

stories.title: Sharks sink Broncos 28-16 at Suncorp — Brisbane's eighth straight loss
stories.why_it_matters: The Sharks beat the Broncos 28-16 at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday night, handing Brisbane their eighth consecutive defeat — a horrendous run that is putting enormous pressure on coach Michael Maguire. Fox Sports is calling for bold decisions from Madge, with the Broncos' season now in serious danger of falling off a cliff. The Sharks, meanwhile, look genuine finals contenders.

stories.title: Eels beat Manly 23-14, handing Sea Eagles a top-four reality check
stories.why_it_matters: Parramatta Eels beat Manly Sea Eagles 23-14 at CommBank Stadium on Sunday afternoon, handing Manly a reality check about their top-four ambitions. Fox Sports reports a veteran Eels player produced a standout highlight-reel moment in the win. The Knights also squeezed past the Dolphins 13-12 in a nail-biter at McDonald Jones Stadium.

stories.title: Alexandra Eala knocks out world No.1 Swiatek at Wimbledon in stunning upset
stories.why_it_matters: Alexandra Eala, a 20-year-old from the Philippines, pulled off one of the biggest Wimbledon upsets in years by defeating Iga Swiatek — the world No.1 — on Saturday. Swiatek had been the heavy favourite and a multiple Grand Slam champion. Meanwhile, Australian No.1 Alex de Minaur has advanced to the second week at Wimbledon, keeping Australian hopes alive in the men's draw. Serena Williams' comeback attempt has stalled again, with the tennis legend failing to progress.

stories.title: AFL: Demons destroy Hawthorn in Tasmania; brawl rocks Round 17
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Demons hammered Hawthorn in Tasmania in what 7NEWS described as a shocking scoreline that stunned the AFL world. Separately, a brawl broke out in another Round 17 match, with players facing scrutiny for making contact with umpires — commentator Kane Cornes called the incident 'pathetic'. GWS Giants also broke a significant win streak when a Fremantle Docker was injured during the match.
